'''''Westringia fruticosa''''', the '''coastal rosemary''' or '''coastal westringia''', is a shrub that grows near the coast in eastern [[Australia]].<ref>[http://apps.kew.org/wcsp/namedetail.do?name_id=214590 Kew World Checklist of Selected Plant Families]</ref>

==Description==
The flowers are white, hairy and have the upper petal divided into two lobes. They also have orange-to-purply spots on their bottom half. This shrub is very tough and grows on cliffs right next to the ocean.

==Cultivation==
The plant's tolerance to a variety of soils, the neatly whorled leaves and  all-year flowering make it very popular in cultivation.<ref>[http://www.anbg.gov.au/gnp/gnp1/westringia-fruticosa.html ANBG - Growing native plants]</ref><ref>[http://www.gardening.eu/plants/Shrubs/Westringia-fruticosa/934/ Gardening Europe]</ref> It (or its cultivar(s)) is a recipient of the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].{{citation needed|date=August 2019}}
